subject: chemistry
question_text: Give the mathematical form of the first law of thermodynamics.

verification.note: Unit 6 Thermodynamics is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack chemistry section (book pp.73-75), which prints the question (as 'Give the mathematical formation of first law of thermodynamics'), its star rank and a model answer. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. This chapter has NO Long Answer section in the book, so no 8-mark form is invented. The 1+1+1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. SIGN CONVENTION: the book's answer takes W as work done BY the system and writes Q = ΔE + W (the older convention). This card writes the NCERT/IUPAC convention ΔU = q + w with w = work done ON the system; the book's version is recorded here, not followed.

steps.label: The law in words
lines: First law of thermodynamics: energy can
neither be created nor destroyed; it can
only change from one form to another.
The total energy of the universe is
steps.why: The equation only records this sentence in symbols: any energy a system gains must arrive as heat or as work.
common_mistakes: Confusing the first law (energy conservation) with the second law (entropy increase).
steps.memory_tip: First law: the total energy stays the same; only its form changes.
steps.margin_note: One or two lines; the remaining marks sit in the equation.

steps.label: Meaning of q and w
lines: Let the system absorb heat q from the
surroundings, and let w be the work done
Both q and w bring energy into the system,
so both count as positive when they do.
steps.why: The equation needs its sign convention stated first: q is positive for heat absorbed, w is positive for work done on the system. The source book instead takes W as work done by the system (the older convention) and writes Q = ΔE + W — the same physics with the sign of the work term reversed.
common_mistakes: Mixing the two conventions in one answer — with w as work done on the system the sign is plus; with work done by the system it is minus.
Leaving q and w undefined and writing the equation bare.
steps.memory_tip: In the NCERT convention both q and w are energy given to the system, so both enter with plus signs.
steps.margin_note: State whose work w is — done on the system — before writing the equation.

steps.label: The equation
lines: The internal energy rises by both
For expansion against a constant external
steps.why: An expanding gas pushes the surroundings outward, so the work done on the system is negative — w = −p(ext)ΔV — while compression makes w positive.
common_mistakes: Writing w = +p(ext)ΔV for expansion — for an expanding gas the work done on it is negative.
Writing ΔU = q − w while also calling w the work done on the system.
steps.memory_tip: Expansion: the system gives out work, so its w is negative. Compression: w is positive.
steps.margin_note: ΔU = q + w is the required form; the expansion case shows the sign working.

steps.label: Special cases
lines: ΔU = 0 — its internal energy is constant.

lines.text: ΔU = q + w, with w = work done on the system

steps.why: The special cases show the equation working: heat supplied at constant volume measures ΔU directly, and an isolated system's internal energy cannot change.
common_mistakes: Writing qp instead of qv for the constant-volume case — qp measures ΔH, not ΔU.
steps.memory_tip: Constant volume: no expansion work, so all the heat goes into internal energy.
steps.margin_note: Box the equation with its convention written beside it.

insider_note: Signs are where this answer is lost. Say once that w is work done on the system and every sign follows; the book's own printed answer uses the older work-done-by convention Q = ΔE + W.
